contexts.description: Admin panel with access gate, server actions for loop management, and JSON API route for loop state; plus the Atlas data-quality scorecard page with its JSON API, and the Data releases page with manifest and snapshot API routes. AdminGate enforces authorization before any admin action. These surfaces expose operational control plane and data layer metadata to trusted operators.
contexts.name: admin-infrastructure

contexts.description: Internal admin surface (/admin) for operating the platform's data-analysis loop: mission-control UI, per-loop progress grids, loop-state machine (driveState/driveLog), tripwire alerts, and vault-heads monitoring. getLoopState.ts reads the persisted loop-run records; loopsJson.ts serialises the loop registry; the loops/ sub-module owns state transitions and idempotent log writes. Not publicly indexed.
contexts.name: admin-observability

contexts.description: Provides the top-level Next.js App Router shell: root layout, global CSS tokens, error boundaries, 404 page, robots/sitemap metadata, OG image, and the landing page entry point. Also co-locates static legal pages (privacy policy, terms of service) that share the shell layout but carry no dynamic data. Depends on features/landing and features/shell for all substantive rendering.
contexts.name: app-shell

contexts.description: Cross-cutting app utilities: URL routing helpers (int/PSP-ID/search-param extractors, live-URL builder), internationalisation config and locale resolution for next-intl, and a security layer (admin gate, token verification). These are server-safe utilities consumed by thin page routes and feature loaders across all modules.
contexts.name: app-utilities

contexts.description: BudgetMirror (/rozpocty) — 132 Czech towns' budget data from the MONITOR series, with peer-group comparison, supplier trail, and a money-trail section linking municipal spending to politically-connected suppliers. mirrorData.ts builds the per-town budget snapshot; peerGroups.ts assigns towns to comparable cohorts; supplierTrail resolves the contractor graph. Generated data files (budgetSnapshots, municipalSuppliers) are pre-computed artefacts.
contexts.name: budget-mirror

contexts.description: Shared write-path infrastructure for all case loops: the props-merge-only `persist-batch` orchestrator, the insert-capable `apply-batch` generalisation, and a `backfill-citations` sweep. Also holds shared ordering utilities and kiosek payload construction helpers used across money and tender loops.
contexts.name: case-loops-core

contexts.description: Implements the census ratchet: a rule-engine that checks whether reader-facing surfaces import only from the shared component library rather than reaching into feature folders or lib/civic. The engine walks the source tree, applies adoption rules from rules.json, and exits non-zero on violations. Self-test and fixture trees provide regression coverage.
contexts.name: census-quality-gate

contexts.description: Deník republiky (/denik) — the chronological dated-record feed and RSS/JSON feed endpoints. deriveDenik.ts assembles time-ordered entries from kg_node facts; feedCodecs.ts serialises them to RSS/JSON; kindLabels assigns human-readable Czech kind labels; limitNotes enforces the per-request entry cap. Consumed by the landing page's DenikTeaser and by external feed subscribers.
contexts.name: civic-chronicle

contexts.description: Dukazy (/dukazy) — an evidence-chain feed surface that exposes the underlying proof graph for reported findings: individual evidence nodes, chain rows, and review-audit trails. deriveFeed.ts assembles ordered evidence chains from kg_node/kg_edge; feedCodecs serialise them to external formats; readReviewAudit.ts records editorial engagement with each evidence packet for audit purposes.
contexts.name: civic-evidence

contexts.description: Labelled fallback sample data for all five modules (lib/civic/), the claim-provenance system that ensures every rendered number cites its source (lib/claims/), Czech number/date formatting (lib/format.ts), and client-side analytics (lib/analytics.ts). Loaders return null on failure; surfaces fall back to this labelled mock data rather than silently rendering fiction.
contexts.name: civic-fallback-data

contexts.api_surface: GET /denik/feed.json, GET /denik/feed.xml, GET /dukazy/feed.json, GET /dukazy/feed.xml, GET /schranka/feed.json, GET /schranka/feed.xml, GET /schranka/novinky.json
contexts.description: Thin route pages and feed API handlers for the Deník (dated record), Důkazy (evidence), Schránka (follow list), Ověření (claim gate), and Zdroj (citation permalink) surfaces. JSON and XML feeds are served as Next.js route handlers alongside their corresponding UI pages, enabling RSS consumption. All substantive rendering is delegated to features/denik, features/schranka, and features/overeni.
contexts.name: civic-feed-routes

contexts.description: Schranka (/schranka) — a zero-account follow list: users subscribe to entities via localStorage keys; the server derives deltas between the stored snapshot and today's facts; feeds are served per-subscriber without authentication. useSchranka/useNews hooks manage client-side state; telemetryScrub strips PII before any analytics; visitWindow tracks recency for delta relevance.
contexts.name: civic-inbox

contexts.description: CivicScore computation engine: the composite contribution formula and its sub-pillars (trend, legacy, citations, legibility), score quality gating, workhorse flavour classification, tenure period copy, atlas data-quality scoring, rapporteur load, context model/provider for score derivation, and JSON-block structured output. This is the authoritative formula implementation imported by /metodika and consumed by /zebricek and /poslanec.
contexts.name: civic-score-computation

contexts.description: Civic Claim Gate (/overeni, /zdroj) — allows anyone to paste a claim or citation and have it re-derived against today's knowledge-graph record. verdict.ts runs the derivation and returns a structured verdict; refDetect.ts recognises claim-reference patterns; liveFigures.ts resolves the figures cited in a claim to their current graph values. VerdictFocus renders the result with full provenance.
contexts.name: civic-verification

contexts.description: The CivicScore leaderboard (/zebricek) that ranks 207 MPs by composite score, supports reader-adjustable lens weights, kraj filtering, and fulltext search. getLeaderboardData fetches ranked MPs from the knowledge graph; lens.ts computes adjusted rankings from weight sliders; componentDefs/componentFill build the per-pillar display data. Drives the landing-page standings and the Souboj duel entry point.
contexts.name: civicscore-leaderboard

contexts.description: The scoring methodology surface (/metodika) and Souboj head-to-head duel feature for CivicScore. MetodikaPage imports every formula constant from lib/analysis/contribution.ts (never literals); duel.ts resolves a URL-encoded MP pair, runs the comparative scoring, and derives the verdict rung. Provenance and score-claim machinery ensures every displayed figure carries a verifiable source reference.
contexts.name: civicscore-scoring

contexts.description: Standalone NPM package providing Czech-specific civic data normalization utilities. Handles UNL (Unified National Location) identifiers, ZIP code validation and formatting, and general entity normalization for Czech political and geographic data. Used by ingest adapters to canonicalize source data before it enters the knowledge graph.
contexts.name: czech-civic-data

contexts.description: The data-model and state layer powering the Velín dashboard: derives dated facts from graph nodes, measures feed relevance and freshness, traverses the knowledge-graph for the state-slice canvas, and exposes a publicWire API. stateSlice.ts builds the per-module readiness snapshot; graphTraversal.ts walks kg_node/kg_edge to populate feed rows. Consumed by dashboard-instruments page components.
contexts.name: dashboard-feed-logic

contexts.description: The Velín (/dashboard) instrument panel that presents module-state tiles, a dated-fact feed, a graph-feed panel, and the leaderboard ledger in a single operator view. Page orchestration and all UI components live here; the server loader (getDashboardData) pre-fetches the graph slice and exhibit metadata and passes typed props to the client feature. Depends on the shared knowledge graph and civicscore leaderboard data.
contexts.name: dashboard-instruments

contexts.description: Data releases page (/data) and Atlas quality scorecard (/atlas) — the platform's transparency layer for its own data. DataReleasesPage publishes the release train and feed address book; manifest.ts maintains the canonical list of released datasets; snapshot.ts tracks dataset staleness. AtlasPage scores each data source for completeness and recency; sealTables.test.ts asserts that every table has a declared retention and ownership.
contexts.name: data-releases-atlas

contexts.description: Low-level PGlite engine internals: DDL application, WAL durability contract, checkpoint maintenance, store copy, schema premigration, query instrumentation, mapper utilities, and the sentinel queue for ordered writes. This is the persistence substrate beneath the repositories — no business logic, only engine reliability.
contexts.name: db-pglite-engine

contexts.description: Repository layer over PGlite — typed read/write functions for every domain table: knowledge-graph nodes/edges, votes, changes, reviews, weights, provenance, ledger entries, and analysis results. Each repository wraps SQL in a typed function consumed by server-only loaders; tests exercise bitemporal correctness and truncation guards.
contexts.name: db-repositories

contexts.description: Provides the single-connection PGlite embedded Postgres store that the entire app reads from. Manages store lifecycle (open, readiness checks, config, read-cap throttle), loader failure logging, migration coordination, and the ordered KG promotion queue. All server-only loaders call getStore()/storeReady() from this context.
contexts.name: db-store-engine

contexts.description: Database maintenance CLI scripts (backup, restore, migration, accounting) plus a standalone benchmark suite that measures PGlite/SQLite query performance for graph traversal, FTS, OLAP aggregations, and vector similarity. The benchmark has its own package.json because it pins a different SQLite build for comparison. Migration helper generates the next DDL migration file from CORE_DDL diff.
contexts.name: db-tooling

contexts.description: MP contribution-effort scoring pipeline: deterministic substrate (tenure, PSP9 contribution, rapporteur load), outlier triage vs club baselines, army input/output extraction, and a gate that enforces public-copy + committee-claims + score-citation invariants before a batch is persisted. Archive subfolder holds one-shot batch probes (pass42, batch-008 through batch-010) kept runnable but never modified.
contexts.name: effort-scoring-tools

contexts.description: Thin route pages for the Volby (elections mirror) and BudgetMirror modules: the flagship voter lookup surface with obec/kraj/sněmovna breakdowns, region (kraj) index and detail pages, and municipal budget pages by IČO. The Volby surface is the primary citizen-facing entry point for local election accountability. All rendering is delegated to features/volby, features/budget, and related loaders.
contexts.name: elections-budget-routes

contexts.description: Publishable ESLint plugin implementing nine custom lint rules that enforce the platform's transparency and code-quality doctrine. Rules cover hardcoded-color prevention, source-citation requirements, server/client import boundaries, silent-error suppression, accessibility (reduced-motion, role-button keydown), and raw-number display. These rules are the machine-checkable expression of the platform's brand and architecture constraints.
contexts.name: eslint-plugin-civic-transparency-rules

contexts.description: Test suite and rule documentation for the eslint-plugin-civic-transparency package. Each of the nine rules has a dedicated test file exercising valid and invalid patterns, plus a Markdown doc stating the rule's rationale and usage. The test runner (run-all.mjs) verifies all rules pass before the package can be published or consumed by the main repo.
contexts.name: eslint-plugin-civic-transparency-tests

contexts.description: Compat shim layer for the nine custom ESLint rules that enforce Politicas' transparency contract: source citations on every rendered number, token-only colors, Czech number formatting, server/client import boundaries, and accessibility guards. Each `.cjs` file is a one-line shim that re-exports the canonical implementation from `packages/eslint-plugin-civic-transparency/`; two rules carry inline test suites. These rules are the mechanical gate between authored code and the brand rule that every figure must cite its source.
contexts.name: eslint-transparency-rules

contexts.description: FollowTheMoney analysis: KG money-edge classification and state machine (kgMoneyStates), money-feed derivation and retry, public-body identification, and public-copy generation for money tie copy. These modules drive the tie ledger, conflict-of-interest detection, and the re-ingest pipeline that refreshes financial verdicts when source data changes.
contexts.name: financial-analysis

contexts.description: Thin route pages for the FollowTheMoney module: main money tie ledger, individual MP money packages, company (firma) profiles by IČO, corruption cases (kauzy), conflicts of interest (střety), and the review console (kontrola). Each route sets metadata and mounts features/money components. Loading skeletons are co-located for streaming UX.
contexts.name: financial-money-routes

contexts.description: The whole-graph interactive canvas (/graf) and its visual rendering stack: stage layout, node/edge glyph rendering, viewport culling, view transforms, arrowhead geometry, and the eight overlay components (NodeInspector, TrailFinder, ForensicOverlays, etc.). VariantMapa and VariantTrasy are layout presets; useNodeSelection manages hover/click state; edgeGate enforces which edge types are visible. The permalink (/graf/p/[ref]) page is included as it shares the same stage.
contexts.name: graph-canvas

contexts.description: The graph-explorer data layer: graph loader (queries kg_node/kg_edge for the canvas), action-settle pipeline (handles user navigation actions and updates the staged subgraph), trail-path finding, diff views for comparing graph snapshots, forensic-view derivation, and the permalink serialisation/deserialisation logic. Also includes test-coverage helpers (catalogParity, oneDefinition) that enforce the stage's API contract.
contexts.name: graph-data-logic

contexts.description: In-process hybrid query engine for benchmarking complex graph analytics that cross the SQL/in-memory boundary: joins, semantic set operations, aggregate operators, tag materialisation, and derived metrics. The engine drives reproducible performance experiments against the embedded database to validate query design decisions before promoting them to production loaders.
contexts.name: hybrid-bench

contexts.description: Core ingestion pipeline utilities: change-event production and keying, document text extraction with PDF sidecar caching (unpdf), normalisation helpers, ZIP decompression, and UNL/member record parsers. These are consumed by the source adapters in ingest-sources-* to turn raw downloads into typed domain records.
contexts.name: ingest-pipeline

contexts.api_surface: smlouvy.gov.cz API, ISVZ API, MONITOR series, dataor.cz, kiosek asset declarations
contexts.description: Source adapters for Czech public-money open data: smlouvy.gov.cz contract registry (live API and bulk XML dump), ISVZ procurement system, dataor.cz court/insolvency data, kiosek asset declarations (including PDF extraction), and MONITOR municipal budget series. These adapters feed the FollowTheMoney and BudgetMirror modules.
contexts.name: ingest-sources-financial

contexts.api_surface: PSP open-data feeds, volby.cz electoral data
contexts.description: Source adapters for Czech parliamentary and electoral open data: PSP (Chamber of Deputies) member/activity/legislation feeds, the pumper batch driver, electoral results (volby), and cross-cutting utilities like exponential backoff and refusal classification. These adapters fetch, parse and normalize raw government data into typed domain records.
contexts.name: ingest-sources-legislative

contexts.api_surface: DataHub GMS HTTP API (publisher); lite-serve exposes DataHub-compatible read endpoints; CLI: da:slice-stats, da:sync, da:forensics
contexts.description: Read-only analysis tooling and the DataHub Lite catalog layer for the knowledge-graph pipeline. slice-stats.ts computes deterministic per-source/entity statistics passed to analyst subagents; kg-forensics.ts orchestrates law-change forensic context preparation and verdict ingestion (Case ③); kg-metrics.ts renders pass-level flywheel curves. The DataHub cluster (datahub-sync, kg-datahub-sync, datahubAspects, dh-context, lite-serve, ab-datahub) publishes corpus metadata to a lightweight HTTP catalog and A/B-tests the metalayer against direct context assembly — metadata only, no civic rows leave the store. validate-verdict.ts and promote-verdicts.ts gate and land data-analysis subagent scores.
contexts.name: kg-analysis-and-catalog

contexts.api_surface: CLI scripts: --commit, --term=PSP10, --refetch flags; Hlídač REST API consumer (HLIDAC_API_TOKEN)
contexts.description: Ingests civic domain data from psp.cz bulk dumps and external APIs into the knowledge graph. Covers the full domain surface: law-amendment bills and e-Sbírka statute registry (legislation), MP contribution scores (effort), FollowTheMoney money ties via Hlídač API (finance), bill roles/engagement (floor speeches, amendments, rapporteur), committee routing, and vote-to-bill spine edges. Each pass is merge-preserving — it reads existing node props before writing — and guarded by pspDump.ts (shared cached downloader).
contexts.name: kg-domain-ingest

contexts.description: Knowledge graph utility library: node/edge glyph type registry, force-directed layout computation, graph provenance (origin tracking and reporting), property registry (the prop-registry.json schema), and source-link resolution. These utilities drive both the /graf canvas and the graph edges rendered in the MP profile and money modules.
contexts.name: kg-graph-utilities

contexts.api_surface: CLI scripts: --commit flag to write, --verdict/--verdicts for promote
contexts.description: Builds and maintains the knowledge graph's computed node/edge layer (kg_node/kg_edge). kg-compute derives deterministic structural edges (co_votes_with, rebels_against, influential_in) from raw ballots; kg-promote gates and lands LLM-proposed interpretive verdicts; maintenance passes (provenance-backfill, repair-orphans, props-check, contribution-recompute) keep schema and provenance contracts consistent. All writers default to dry-run and require --commit to write.
contexts.name: kg-graph-writers

contexts.description: Thin route pages and API handlers for the graph canvas explorer, citation permalink cards with OG image generation and bundle API, the archived Rentgen art-direction lab (noindex), a referendum surface, and the Svědectví (witness testimony) page. The graf routes power the whole-graph playground and permalink sharing; the remaining pages are experimental or archival surfaces outside the main module set.
contexts.name: labs-graph-routes

contexts.description: Archived Rentgen art direction (/rentgen, noindex) — a fixed-hex design exploration that served as the runner-up direction before Konstrukt was chosen. terminalModel.ts drives the terminal-style display; getTerminalData loads the specimen data. Kept as a living reference; hardcoded colours are intentionally permitted here. No imports from this module are expected by other contexts.
contexts.name: labs-rentgen

contexts.description: The Konstrukt-design landing page (/) that surfaces the real-time CivicScore leaderboard, hemicycle visualisation, and cross-module specimen ride. It orchestrates hero story, standings, source panel and module tiles, reading live data via server loaders and falling back to labelled civic mocks. Depends on the shared leaderboard loader, format utilities, and design-token palette.
contexts.name: landing-core

contexts.description: A sub-surface off the landing page for civic referendum polling — captures voter responses, aggregates totals, and exposes embeddable OG/social payloads. Actions write vote records and loaders re-derive the published aggregate; the embed module serialises a shareable card from the live tally. Depends on the PGlite store via the referendum loader.
contexts.name: landing-referendum

contexts.description: Amended-paragraph census pipeline (amends-census → amends-regen → apply → validate → diff), e-Sbírka SPARQL and streaming adapters for live law versions, bill text extraction (tiskText), provenance probes, corpus builders (summaries, CZ verdicts, missing-law ingest), and read-only inspectors. This is the data-acquisition and enrichment arm of the LawWatch case loop.
contexts.name: law-amends-corpus

contexts.description: Archived one-shot diagnostic probes for LawWatch batches 002–012: early amends-regen validation runs, initial collision-check iterations (passes 005–009), ledger rebase, duplicate-bill detection, and precision measurement scripts. Kept runnable with relative imports repointed to `../` but never modified after their batch closed.
contexts.name: law-archive-early

contexts.description: Archived one-shot diagnostic probes for LawWatch batches 013–021: sector adjacency, paragraph-level sector attribution, evidence-coordinate scanning and applying, old-27 law extraction, dependency census, and prepare-batch iterations 013–021. Includes the `_apply-missing-law-nodes-copy` correction script kept for its rule documentation.
contexts.name: law-archive-late

contexts.description: Forensic severity ranking of 141 bills (triage core), bill-pair collision detection, cause-collapse grouping, verdict/citation scope guards, sector attribution for companies, and batch preparation for army verdict runs. ARMY-CONTRACT.md is the brief every verdict agent receives. These are the durable gating and classification tools for the LawWatch case loop.
contexts.name: law-triage-collision

contexts.description: LawWatch bill surfaces (/zakony, /zakony/[id], statute registry, collisions page) that track 141 bills through to 101 enacted laws, maintain the forensic register of sponsoring MPs, attribute bills to sectors, and surface kolize (conflict-of-interest overlaps). Multiple server loaders query the knowledge graph per surface; deriveStatuteDossier builds the per-statute case view; forensicIndex.ts assembles the ordered register.
contexts.name: lawwatch-bills

contexts.description: The legislative radar feed and sector-attribution layer within LawWatch: derives a rolling radar of recently-progressed bills, attributes them to policy sectors, produces RSS-compatible feed codecs, and computes dependency relationships between bills. deriveRadar.ts assembles the radar from the knowledge graph; sectorAttribution.ts applies taxonomy rules; getDependencyData builds the dependency graph used by DependencyRadar.
contexts.name: lawwatch-radar

contexts.description: Archived one-shot diagnostic probes for the FollowTheMoney case loop (batches b9–b14): ownership chain building, public-mandate classification, direction triage and refinement, stale-ICO detection, party state snapshots, and batch-specific validators. Superseded tools are noted in the active README (e.g. `dataor-ownership-chains` replaced by `ownership-sweep`).
contexts.name: money-archive-probes

contexts.api_surface: External: Registr smluv API, kiosek úřední desky
contexts.description: Registr smluv contract ingestion and tie triage: bulk-dump harvest, live party-search sweeps (company, parent, Agrofert), smlouvy retry logic, payload schema validation, surface verification against `getMoneyData()`, and corpus census tools (supplies coverage, reachable metric audit, corpus snapshot). Kiosek úřední-desky watch also lives here.
contexts.name: money-contracts

contexts.description: The evidence, tie-classification, and conflict-of-interest (střety) layer for FollowTheMoney. Classifies financial ties by type and temporal validity; resolves ownership chains; calculates the set of money reachable via the graph; and surfaces the střety (conflicts-of-interest) page where vote alignments are cross-referenced against procurement ties. collisions/ sub-module overlaps with lawwatch kolize detection.
contexts.name: money-evidence

contexts.description: MP and company case-file surfaces (/penize/pos/[id], /penize/firma/[id]) plus evidence-packet dossiers. Each case file aggregates financial ties, ownership chains, and contract histories into a structured dossier; getLeadDossiers discovers the most-significant leads; the review summary/actions pipeline manages the editorial review workflow for flagged ties. Depends on money-evidence for tie classification and ownership resolution.
contexts.name: money-investigations

contexts.description: FollowTheMoney core surface (/penize) — the tie ledger, money graph, Kauzy page, and review verification console. getMoneyData queries the knowledge graph for financial ties; MoneyGraph renders the interactive force-directed graph; moneyLoader.ts orchestrates the multi-step graph traversal for the main ledger. The components/ sub-tree provides all reusable money-display primitives (TiesLedger, StatTiles, VerificationConsole).
contexts.name: money-ledger

contexts.api_surface: External: ARES VR API, dataor bulk API
contexts.description: Beneficial ownership resolution and verification pipeline: `owns_stake` layer ingestion from dataor bulk and ARES VR, depth-2 exposure analysis, public-mandate verdict computation, legal-form drift audit, and ARES VR period reconciliation. Also includes one-time correction scripts (canonicalize-ico, purge-osvc, prak-repoint) retained as rule documentation.
contexts.name: money-ownership

contexts.description: The Spis MP case file (/poslanec/[id]) that consolidates a politician's CivicScore, six pillar components, absence record, career spine, rebellion history, and money ties into one surface. Server loader (getProfileData) fetches all data from the knowledge graph; rebellion records are derived separately and surfaced with full provenance. Depends on civicscore scoring, money ties, and shared provenance primitives.
contexts.name: mp-profile

contexts.description: Thin Next.js route pages that mount MP-facing feature components: the poslanec case file, CivicScore leaderboard, political compass, print-quality poster view, methodology page, and the Velín dashboard with its exhibit detail. Also includes the embedded leaderboard widget route used for iframe embeds. Each page sets metadata and delegates all rendering to features/profile, features/civicscore, and features/dashboard.
contexts.name: mp-profile-routes

contexts.description: Quality assurance tooling outside the main test gate: the sentinel nightly runner that checks for regressions in computed metrics, KPI citation-coverage and verify-loop meters, a doc-sync checker that validates docs stay coupled to their source files, a copy-check git hook, and a smoke test that exercises the data pipeline end-to-end. These are meters and monitors, not blocking gates.
contexts.name: scripts-quality-gates

contexts.description: Domain-agnostic UI primitive catalog for all reader-facing surfaces: SourceNote (the citation primitive that enforces the brand rule), StatTile, Combobox, DataUnavailable, AnimatedScore, RankDelta, VerdictProvenance, and others. All components carry @catalog JSDoc tags. The forensic/ sub-module (ForensicProvider, ForensicToggle, forensicMode) provides the global forensic-mode context used by overlays across all surfaces. No imports from features/* or lib/civic allowed.
contexts.name: shared-components

contexts.description: Cross-cutting provenance and citation infrastructure: ProvenanceCapsule and ReceiptPage render the canonical proof-chain display for any cited figure; receipt.ts serialises a claim reference into a cryptographically-linkable receipt; claimRef/caseFileLink/asOfLens are navigation helpers for deep-linking into the provenance chain. The poster/ sub-module adds shareable poster frames (PosterFrame, PosterToolbar) and a leaderboard-poster demo. Consumed by overeni, graph, and any surface that cites figures.
contexts.name: shared-provenance

contexts.description: The persistent application chrome mounted in app/layout.tsx: left nav rail, mobile bottom nav, section-anchor tracking, and sitemap/robots metadata. navModel.ts declares all module routes and each page's section anchors; isBareRoute() opts selected pages out of the shell. Page components must not draw their own logo — the shell owns it.
contexts.name: shell-navigation

contexts.description: Top-level app shell components used across all routes. LanguageSwitcher toggles the CS/EN locale by flipping the NEXT_LOCALE cookie via a server action and refreshing the RSC tree in place. MpProfileBeacon is a zero-render analytics beacon that fires a Plausible 'mp-profile-view' event on MP profile mounts, delegating to lib/analytics.ts which silently no-ops without NEXT_PUBLIC_PLAUSIBLE_DOMAIN.
contexts.name: shell-ui-components

contexts.description: Public procurement analysis loop for the Elections & Budget module: maps each zadavatel (contracting authority) to its electoral accountability tier (municipal/regional/parliamentary), computes monopoly and winner-circle flags, measures tender pool statistics, and persists per-month increments. `deep-read.ts` does the close read of individual tender records; `arena.ts` is the authority-to-election bridge.
contexts.name: tender-pipeline

contexts.description: Core test infrastructure: PGlite test fixtures and templates, lane partitioning for parallel test execution, gate-ladder assertions, server-boundary enforcement checks, route-source correctness tests (admin, shell, civic-feed, money, legislation, rankings), revalidate-parity checks, Sentry scrub source verification, and a crash-writer utility for reproducing failures.
contexts.name: testing-core

contexts.description: Two reliability sub-systems for the test suite: the flake registry tracks historically non-deterministic tests (detect, history, registry, sequencer) so they run last and their failures are expected; the sentinel validates app-wide structural invariants (route facts, path oracle, invariant rules) that span multiple modules and cannot be owned by any single feature test.
contexts.name: testing-flake-sentinel

contexts.description: Analysis engine for parliamentary votes and legislation: verdict derivation and provenance, law-bill verdict, KG-level verdict aggregation, committee claim extraction, language-gate filtering, plausible-date validation, club/party membership at a point in time, tripwire invariant checks, and the full election-analysis sub-module (contested seats, regional rules, term boundaries). Drives /hlasovani, /zakony, and /volby.
contexts.name: verdict-and-law-analysis

contexts.description: The Volby election mirror (/volby) — the flagship voter surface: municipality and kraj lookup, ballot-keyed subject cards showing elected party lists, a severity ledger of procurement/conflict findings composed at read time, and a dated outcome timeline. Multiple loaders (getObecData, getKrajData, getListData) serve the hierarchy of obec → kraj → sněmovna pages; tenderLayer overlays procurement findings onto election results.
contexts.name: volby-elections

contexts.description: The Political Compass feature (/hlasovani/kompas) and vote-record analysis layer. Users answer policy questions and their positions are scored against each MP's actual vote record to derive ideological alignment. The record/ sub-module handles vote-outcome derivation, threshold rules, party-discipline reconciliation, and club styling — the shared analytical foundation for both the compass and the rebellion tracking.
contexts.name: votetrack-kompas-analysis

contexts.description: VoteTrack (/hlasovani) — the core vote ledger, chamber hemicycle, discipline board, and seismograf surfaces that display how MPs voted on each bill. Server loaders (getVoteThemes, getVoteRecord) query the knowledge graph; the ledger supports theme filtering and anchor-deep-linking; the Real* components mount live-data equivalents of the mock shells. Relies on record/reconcile for chamber self-reconciliation.
contexts.name: votetrack-ledger

contexts.description: Thin route pages for the VoteTrack and LawWatch modules: the vote ledger and chamber discipline board, individual law detail pages, the regulatory conflict feed, and the legislative predpis (regulation) listing. Feeds for law conflicts are served as JSON and RSS route handlers alongside the UI pages. All rendering is delegated to features/votetrack and features/lawwatch.
contexts.name: voting-legislation-routes
